predictions: Review all6 full source photographs and available edges. Record each candidate mark with exact native coordinates, orientation, literal form and source context before assigning its function.

An original address needs more than numeral-like shape: check original margin position, hand/ink/orientation and relation to the medieval writing. Later account foliation, shelfmarks, photographic rulers, chapter/service numerals, musical dividers and custodes are alternatives.

Do not normalize a musical sign or two strokes into a folio/quire number without evidence. Uncertain or cropped marks remain qualified; a known8994 glyph example does not establish a shared numbering scheme.

Compare addresses only if both source readings and their address conventions are secure. Equal-looking numbers can reset across sections or separate books; different numbers can occupy different leaves in one book.

If no secure comparable address is recovered, record that narrow available-source result, not evidence of different books or an exhaustive absence of original marks. Preserve physical/capture/medieval-side distinctions.
